name: Napeca
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Chapacuran; known only from name/wordlist mentions (Crequi-Montfort & Rivet 1913); no descriptive source

sources.citation: Persée record: de Créqui-Montfort & Rivet 1913, DOI 10.3406/jsa.1913.2851 (article landing page text, first page only; PDF download altcha-protected)
sources.note: Only p.119 visible; content read in full from the archive.org scanned instead.

sources.citation: Birchall, Joshua, Michael Dunn & Simon J. Greenhill. 2016. A combined comparative and phylogenetic analysis of the Chapacuran language family. International Journal of American Linguistics 82(3): 255-284. (open postprint, MPG PuRe item_2332314)
sources.note: Silent on Napeka stress. Sec. 2 item 3 documents the Napeka sources: d'Orbigny wordlist in CM&R 1913, Cardús 1886 (48 items), Jürgen Riester's 1960s field notebook (~50 words) and untranscribed audio of songs/interviews with the last speakers at Concepción; phonological analysis of that material in Wienold 2012 (MA Leipzig, pp.54-62 cited for /ʎ/ and [z]).

sources.citation: Angenot-de Lima, Geralda & Jean-Pierre Angenot. 2000. O sistema prosódico Panchapakura de demarcação lexical (com uma bibliografia das línguas Chapakura). In van der Voort & van de Kerke (eds.), Indigenous Languages of Lowland South America (ILLA 1), 149-164. Leiden: CNWS.
sources.note: Instrumental prosody of 300 cognates in 5 living Chapakura languages; conclusion p.157 repeats the family-wide rule (lexeme stress deducible from syllable weight, prominence on the heavy syllable). Napeka appears only in the bibliography (Cardús 1886; Nimuendajú ms. s.3:f.17). No Napeka data.

sources.citation: Angenot-de Lima, Geralda. 1997. Fonotática e fonologia do lexema Protochapakura. Dissertação de Mestrado, UNIR (Guajará-Mirim). 251 pp.
sources.note: §3.8 pp.52-54 'Fonemas e sons do Napeka' (source: CM&R 1913): phoneme/allophone tables, phonotactics, examples -- no stress statement. §2.2 p.24 family-wide claim: 'Nas línguas Chapakura, a acentuação dos lexemas é dedutível do peso silábico... o acento não é fonológico por ser previsível... /#(σ)σ#/ → [(σ̀)ˈσ́]' (light syllable unstressed/low, heavy syllable stressed/high), grounded in the living languages; p.7 states the six dead languages incl. Napeka 'nunca tiveram seus sistemas fonológicos descritos'. Not a first-hand Napeka statement.

sources.citation: de Créqui-Montfort, Georges & Paul Rivet. 1913. Linguistique bolivienne. La famille linguistique Čapakura. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 10(1): 119-171. (archive.org whole-volume scanned journaldelasocie0010unse; Persée PDF altcha-blocked)
sources.note: Nothing. Reproduces Cardús's Napeka (N) forms in the comparative vocabulary; grammatical notes pp.135-137 (pronouns hual'a/abum/arikó, future infix -ta-, negation infix -za-); transcription conventions referred to their 1912 Otuke paper; no remark on accent for any Čapakura language.

sources.citation: Cardús, José. 1886. Las misiones franciscanas entre los infieles de Bolivia: descripción del estado de ellas en 1883 y 1884... una muestra de varias lenguas. Barcelona: Librería de la Inmaculada Concepción. (image-only scan from Minerva/USC, hdl 10347/19455; pp.304-327 scanned)
sources.note: Nothing. p.308 only: 'Las lenguas paunaca y napeca las hablan dos distintas parcialidades de Concepcion de Chiquitos.' p.320 'Lengua Napeca': numbered list of 48 words/phrases, a few with acute accents (Aricó, Panató); pronunciation notes are given for Guarayo, Mosetén, Yuracaré, Cayubaba etc. but none for Napeca.

sources.citation: d'Orbigny, Alcide. 1839. Voyage dans l'Amérique méridionale, t. IV, 1re partie: L'homme américain (de l'Amérique méridionale). Paris/Strasbourg. (archive.org voyagedanslameri41orbi scanned)
sources.note: Nothing. 'Nation Chapacura' pp.288-290 gives impressionistic sound remarks for Chapacura/Quitémoca (finals mostly vowels, some in c, m, t, p, j; guttural j; nasal u; body-part suffix -chi/-ché); Napeca is not named in this volume; no accent statement.

sources.citation: Wienold, Christin. 2012. The Chapacuran language family: Kitemoka and Napeka. M.A. (Magister) thesis, Universität Leipzig.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Only modern phonological analysis of Napeka (pp.54-62 cited by Birchall et al. 2016), based on Jürgen Riester's 1960s audio recordings of the last speakers; the one place a first-hand stress/accent observation for Napeka could exist.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. n.d. Documentos inéditos, principalmente vocabulários. Arquivos microfilmados do Museu Nacional do Rio de Janeiro, s.3:f.17 (Napeka).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Additional unpublished Napeka vocabulary listed in Angenot-de Lima & Angenot 2000 bibliography; Nimuendajú usually marked stress with accents, so it could give word-level accent placement even without a prose rule.

sources.citation: Riester, Jürgen. 1960s. Field notebook (~50 Napeka words) and audio recordings of Napeka songs and interviews, Concepción (Santa Cruz, Bolivia). Unpublished; partly transcribed in Wienold 2012.

sources.note: The only sound recordings of Napeka; stress placement could be measured directly from the audio if the archive location (Riester estate / APCOB / Leipzig?) can be identified.
